Blog Review: Aug. 5

Shares

PSS 3.1 channels; reset domain crossing; physics becomes critical; feedforward control; latency vs. latency.

August 5th, 2026 -

By: Jesse Allen

Cadence’s Siddh Virani introduces PSS 3.1 channels, which add a standard way to describe target-time communication between running realization code, complementing rather than replacing solver scheduling and flow objects.
Siemens’ Reetika explains why reset domain crossing detection needs to combine structural analysis with timing knowledge to distinguish real design risks from safe implementation choices.
Synopsys’ Larry Williams warns that electrical, thermal, and structural behavior are no longer separable in advanced designs as physics becomes a first-order design constraint.
Lam Research’s Swapnil Kailash More explains why feedforward control helps recover wafers before scrap and how to use simulation to test its effectiveness.
Keysight’s Eric Yu warns that latency can mean two different things in AI data center networks, and confusing them leads to systematic mischaracterization of fabric performance.
Imagination’s Thomas Ferrere introduces a multiprecision dot product unit that accelerates matrix multiplications in a variety of number formats while maintaining accuracy and reducing circuit area.
Arm’s Odin Shen explains why CPU orchestration, memory, and runtime design are key to persistent AI agents, where the challenge is whether the system can continue to exist, respond, remember, retrieve, and behave consistently across components over time.
For a change of pace from reading, why not watch a recent video:
How to achieve a 10X productivity improvement using AI Agent Orchestration For ASIC Autonomy.
Challenges increase significantly with chiplets and coherency when Verifying Networks On Chip.
AI Models On The Edge and how to customize NPUs without sacrificing flexibility.
Complex chips require much more work earlier in the flow, so How Far Left Can You Shift?
New USB Standards: Benefits And Incompatibilities presents a roadmap for integrating different versions of the USB and eUSB.
Will Your Chip’s Memory Work As Expected and how to ensure that memory is fully tested and repaired.
Determining when a complex chip design is ready to be shipped to manufacturing with Signoff Of Synthesis-Optimized Registers.
How agents can be used to divide and conquer IC design problems when Building Multi-Agent Systems For ASIC Flows.
A look inside the next-generation 1 Megawatt Racks In Data Centers.
The Evolution Of UCIe and how the standard matured from simple connectivity to secure data movement across multiple chiplets and packaging approaches.
Moving Defect Detection And Classification To The Edge as the explosion in defectivity requires much faster determination of critical and non-critical defects.
Where the choke points are in AI systems and Overcoming Bottlenecks In Data Movement.
What’s needed to ensure reliability of automotive chips, and why DFT In Automotive is about to get even tougher.
